summary: Nicolaas Johannes Krom worked in Indology and archaeology. He earned his classics Ph.D. at Leiden University (1901–1908), studying under Kern and Speyer. He served at the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (1913–1916) and held a professorship at Leiden (1919–1945).

Linguist Nicolaas van Wijk studied at Amsterdam under Uhlenbeck, Leipzig under Brugmann and Leskien (~1902–1903), and Moscow State University under Fortunatov (~1903–1904). He worked at the National Library of the Netherlands (1907) and became Professor of Slavic and Baltic linguistics at Leiden in 1913.
Working in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, Nicolas Morrissey studied under Gregory Schopen (attested 2004). He holds a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies who studied at Silpakorn University (2012–2013) and was supervised by Claudine Bautze-Picron, Peter Skilling, and Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h. He held a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016–2017).
Nicolas Sihlé, a specialist in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, served as Assistant Professor in the Department of Anthropology at the University of Virginia (attested 2010).

Linguist and Tibetologist Nicolas Tournadre earned his PhD under Claude Hagège at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1987–1992). He held posts at INALCO, Paris 8, the University of Provence (~2004–2011), and became professor of linguistics at Aix-Marseille University in ~2011.
Nicole Baden, active in Buddhist and religious studies, studied under Richard Baker as her traditional teacher and succeeded him in 2024.

Nicole Balbir was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Charlotte Vaudeville. She held positions at Patna University (1952–1955) and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1974–1992).
Active in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history, Nicole Vandier-Nicolas taught Chinese art at the École du Louvre and served as professor of Chinese civilization at INALCO (~1966–1977).

Nicolás Altuchow was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak (~1934–1939). He taught linguistics and occasionally Sanskrit at the University of the Republic (1951–1982) and held a post at the National Museum of Natural History.
Nidheesh Kannan B. is an Indologist who completed his Doctor of Philosophy at Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (2016–2018), where he became an Assistant Professor in 2021.

Niels Ludvig Westergaard worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Copenhagen, Bonn under Christian Lassen, Paris, and Oxford. He served at the University of Copenhagen as Lektor (1844), professor of Indian-oriental philology (1850), and Rector (1867–1868).

Niels Studsgaard Fuglsang, a scholar in Indology, studied at the University of Copenhagen in 1778. He served as Minister at Zion Church in Tranquebar (1792–1804) and became a member of The Asiatic Society in 1801.
Nigel Allan, active in history and archaeology, succeeded Marianne Winder and served as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust (attested 1993).

Niharranjan Ray studied at Calcutta, UCL, and Leiden under Jean Philippe Vogel. He served as Chief Librarian (1936) and Bageswari Professor of Fine Arts (1946–1965) at the University of Calcutta, and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1965–1970).

Nijun Zhang studied at Beijing Foreign Studies University (BA 2018–2022) and the University of Pittsburgh (MA 2023–2025). Focusing on religious studies and Tibetology, Zhang became a PhD student at the University of Virginia in 2025.

Nika Jovic, who specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, completed a Magistra der Philosophie under supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes at the University of Vienna (attested 2010), having also studied under Géza Bethlenfalvy (2007–2008).
Nikita Yakovlevich Bichurin worked in Sinology and Central Asian studies. He was educated at the Kazan Theological Academy and held a post at the Département asiatique from ~1826 to 1853.

Niklas Luhmann was a philosopher who studied at the University of Freiburg (~1946–1949), Harvard University (~1960–1961), and Bielefeld University. He held an academic post at Bielefeld University from ~1968 to 1993.
Niklas Müller was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1786–1788). In 1805, he became Conservator at the Städtische Kunstsammlungen Mainz.
